title: ALMA sub-mm maser and dust distribution of VY Canis Majoris
question: Where do the 658, 321 and 325 GHz water masers lie relative to the star VY CMa and its dust continuum, and do they match excitation model predictions?

what.value: Dust and wind density/velocity profiles for VY CMa used in maser excitation model

evidence.quote: based upon the density and velocity profiles obtained for VY CMa by Decin et al. (2006)
We adopted the latest quantal rate coefficients (Daniel et al. 2011)

what.value: Literature continuum flux densities for comparison

evidence.quote: We compared the total continuum flux densities with literature values (Fu et al 2012; Kamiński et al. 2013; Muller et al. 2007; Shinnaga et a. 2004).

external_data.citation: Fu et al 2012; Kamiński et al. 2013; Muller et al. 2007; Shinnaga et al. 2004

recipe.method: Standard ALMA calibration with Pallas flux scale, J0522-3627 bandpass, J0648-3044 phase reference; self-cal on brightest maser channel
Natural-weighted continuum; continuum-subtracted maser cubes with robust=0.5
2D Gaussian fits per channel; components >3σ (321, 325) or >4σ (658), at least three successive channels
Collisional excitation, radiative decay, escape-probability trapping with steep velocity gradient; negative optical depth contours vs T and n(H2)

evidence.loc: VY CMa continuum and maser morphology
